free_text: Clients send me photos of receipts and invoices on Viber, about 200 a month, and I type every one into Excel. That's roughly 6 hours a week. Then I chase the ones who forget to send their documents before the 5th.
Every month I put together a short summary of income and expenses for each of my 12 clients. Documents arrive everywhere: email, Viber, Telegram, and I first have to sort out what belongs to whom.

Clients keep asking me the same things: which documents I need for the quarter, when the deadline is, how much the service costs. And sometimes a client disputes an expense I booked and we argue about whether it's deductible.

free_text: I write a commercial proposal for almost every new client, usually from scratch, 3–4 a week. Then I follow up if they go quiet after a few days.
Every Friday I build the sales funnel report for my boss from the CRM export and explain why the numbers dropped or grew compared to last week.
Clients ask for discounts all the time, and I have to decide case by case whether we can go lower. I also answer the same questions about delivery terms and payment by email.
I'm also updating my CV and going to two interviews this month because I want to switch jobs. At work I mostly copy leads from Telegram into a Google Sheet.
My inbox, WhatsApp and Telegram all have client messages, and I lose track of who asked what. Then I schedule demo calls with each one, which is a lot of back and forth.
I run a small café. People write in Instagram DMs about bookings, opening hours and whether we have vegan options. I answer them till late at night, maybe 5 hours a week.
Every week I make the shift schedule for 8 baristas, and everyone has wishes: who can't work mornings, who wants weekends off. It takes me about 3 hours.
I own a beauty salon. Suppliers send me price lists in Excel and I compare them to see what got more expensive. I also write the weekly newsletter with our offers.
A customer left a 1-star review saying our coffee made her sick, and I need to decide what to do about it. Usually I reply to reviews myself.
At the end of each week I look at sales from the POS system and write a short summary for my business partner: how many coffees, which desserts sold, what we wasted.

Delivery notes from suppliers come as paper photos and I type the quantities and prices into my stock sheet. Also people who order cakes on Facebook — I write each order into a notebook so I don't forget.
